decisive_spans.text: completed a course of prostate-directed radiation therapy with a SpaceOAR hydrogel spacer
large deep-cratered solitary ulcer on the anterior rectal wall with firm margins, friability, and exudate

response.rationale: The patient's history of prostate-directed radiation therapy and the presence of a rectal ulcer strongly support a radiation-induced etiology. D5 (Chronic radiation-induced rectal ulcer) is the most specific and accurate diagnosis, encompassing both the cause and the finding. D4 (Radiation Proctitis) is also highly supported but less specific than D5, as proctitis refers to inflammation of the rectum, while D5 specifically names the ulcer. D2 (Chronic Radiation Injury) is a broader term and less specific than D5. D1 (Rectal adenocarcinoma) is contradicted by negative biopsies for malignancy.
